outcome: After process interruption, Sworn reconciles owned implementation work before abandoned-workspace cleanup, restoring the last durable checkpoint or preserving attributable interrupted files as explicitly unverified recovery data.

acceptance.text: Kill the driving process after a production worker has written scoped code but before a valid submission. After the old worker is proved quiescent and the normal ownership boundary permits takeover, the replacement owner does not delete the sole attributable workspace before reconciliation. Retained interrupted bytes or the last durable checkpoint are available to the authorized continuation without another implementation write recreating them. Anchor: extend test/e2e/exactly_once_linux_test.go and test/e2e/detached_drive_linux_test.go with a worker write barrier and inspect actual Git/journal state.

Exercise crash cuts around durable workspace attribution, checkpoint content preparation, durable checkpoint binding, retention publication and workspace cleanup. Each restart converges idempotently; an unbound object is never reported as a completed checkpoint, a bound object remains reachable, and successful recovery does not duplicate a candidate or transition. Anchor: test/e2e/exactly_once_linux_test.go and internal/gitx/workspaces_test.go recovery fixtures.

A live or ambiguously live prior worker, ownership mismatch, foreign repository/run attribution, or corrupt recovery binding prevents concurrent restoration or execution. No second writer enters the track, and the original recoverable data is not discarded to make the refusal disappear. Anchor: test/e2e/topology_recovery_linux_test.go takeover fencing and workspace writer-lock tests.

Changed plan/contract/base or target authority prevents automatic restoration into the new authority. The prior checkpoint remains inspectable as stale, unverified work with its provenance and a specific reason; it does not become a current candidate. Anchor: test/e2e/track_base_linux_test.go and test/e2e/topology_recovery_linux_test.go authority-movement cases.

Report the actual durability boundary: a completed checkpoint guarantees its measured bytes; salvaged files from an interrupted write may be partial and must be labeled unverified. Sudden power loss during an unacknowledged filesystem write is not represented as zero-loss recovery. Anchor: built-product interrupted-write case, board/status output and docs/run.md.

constraints: One existing command service and journal own durable transitions; reuse existing workspace ownership, Git measurement, effect recovery and candidate submission boundaries. Introduce new representation only where an unverified checkpoint cannot truthfully use an existing candidate or receipt.

A saved checkpoint is unverified product data, never a candidate admission, check PASS, Captain decision, Verifier verdict, plan approval, or permission to merge. Only the established exact candidate and independent verification path can grant those states.

Do not execute or source retained files during measurement or restoration. Exclude .git metadata, reserved records roots, invocation scratch, engine/provider credential locations and existing secret-exclusion paths, and non-product runtime files. This does not claim to detect arbitrary secrets embedded in scoped source code. Existing scope, filesystem and resource policies remain enforced.
Model and driver selection stay explicit with no fallback. Do not persist provider credentials or assume a conversation can survive process death.

The checks list declares host obligations. Every listed check is a host_check: contained implementers and verifiers consume engine-bound host evidence and must never attempt nested containment or claim to have executed these commands. Run the long process suites once per candidate in the listed sequence; a candidate change requires fresh applicable evidence.

The broad supporting package scope admits only this promised mechanism and its affected regression fixtures, adapters, status projections and documentation. It grants no unrelated refactor, provider selection, verification relaxation, or new orchestration policy.

Preserve normal operation of valid existing journals and candidates that predate checkpoints. Missing or ambiguous legacy checkpoint provenance limits salvage of the affected workspace only; it neither invalidates the whole historical journal nor fabricates checkpoint evidence.

Operator context from the superseded run 2026-09-05-preserve-work-recovery (three consecutive gemini-3.8-flash implementation tries, each ending INVOCATION_TIMEOUT at 60 minutes, each starting a fresh conversation): its unverified checkpoints remain anchored as stale reference under refs/heads/checkpoints/2026-09-05-preserve-work/T1-preservation/ (commits 09b237b5, 3965416d, a2c43228, all against design base 0f61e534). They may be inspected for the attribution/adoption shape they reached; they are not a candidate, must not be restored or copied wholesale, and their failing self-authored tests are not evidence of anything. Design from this contract and the Captain-corrected design first.

Known contained-workspace facts, not defects of this slice: cmd/sworn's TestTUIActionDriveSurvivesActionReturn fails in the sandbox with CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE and prints roughly 90 KB of DEBUG output; it passes on the host. Do not chase it and do not run it in the workspace (exclude it with -skip or -run, or rely on host evidence). internal/runtime exceeds Go's implicit 10-minute package deadline in the sandbox; pass -timeout=20m on your own package runs. The sandbox shell is dash without `which`. Never build a binary into the workspace root (for example `go build ./test/e2e/testdata/fake` writes ./fake): an out-of-scope file at the root makes checkpoint capture refuse with CHECKPOINT_SCOPE_VIOLATION and fences the workspace; build into a temporary directory.

Known seam from the superseded tries: a crash cut at workspace cleanup or checkpoint publication left the replacement owner at the existing effect-recovery refusal (board: Needs confirmation, Sworn cannot confirm whether the last external action finished), the detached-drive takeover case returned CONTROL_REJECTED, and the topology case hit journal DATABASE_FAILED. Reconciliation must be bound as a recoverable effect through the existing crash-cut injection convention (SWORN_TEST_CRASH_AFTER_EFFECT, per Captain correction 5) so that each restart converges rather than asking for confirmation.
